_comment: Threshold requirements, Iowa 2026-2027 Second Amended 9% QAP. Section 3 Eligibility (PDF pp.13-19) at the level of its numbered and lettered requirements, plus the Section 4 underwriting limits that bear on scoring or feasibility (pp.20-23). Not extracted: Section 2 application process mechanics, the remainder of Section 4 (contingencies, appraisals, ineligible basis items, operating assumptions), and Part B post-reservation requirements. Iowa states no minimum score.

criteria.heading: Legal ownership entity; qualified contract waiver
criteria.quote: The Ownership Entity shall waive the right to a qualified contract

criteria.heading: Qualifying entity
criteria.quote: At least one Developer or General Partner/Managing Member, and Affiliates thereof, of
criteria.note: The Developer or GP/MM must already serve in that role on a tax credit project that has received an 8609, and a Developer acting as Qualifying Entity must receive at least 50% of the developer and consultant fee. Developers new to Iowa are addressed in 3.2.C.

criteria.heading: Ineligibility of development team members
criteria.quote: INELIGIBILITY. Any QDT member or Affiliates thereof may be deemed ineligible by the Director to
criteria.note: Twelve grounds, A-L, from financial crime to an uncorrected 8823 or a returned full credit allocation.

criteria.heading: Site requirements: incorporated city, no alternate sites
criteria.quote: The proposed Project shall be in an incorporated city at Application submission.

criteria.heading: Zoning in place at application
criteria.note: Special use permits and variances must already be approved at submission. The quote is short because the sentence breaks across a line; it sits in the zoning paragraph on p.15.

criteria.heading: Site control
criteria.quote: Options to purchase or lease must be valid for at least nine months
criteria.note: Recorded deed, exclusive purchase option or contract with the fee owner, or a lease of at least 35 years.

criteria.heading: Minimum set-aside election
criteria.note: 20-50, 40-60 or Average Income. The Average Income Test is closed to scattered sites, projects with market-rate units and projects with a project-based rental assistance contract, which bears on 6.1.D.1, 6.1.E and 6.1.F.

criteria.heading: No market-rate single-family homes
criteria.quote: Market-rate single-family homes shall not be allowed.

criteria.heading: Displacement of residential tenants
criteria.quote: IFA may reject any Application that fails to minimize
criteria.note: A formal relocation plan is required wherever the scope needs temporary or permanent relocation.

criteria.heading: Developer fee limit
criteria.quote: Remaining Units within the Project above 24
criteria.note: 18% for the first 24 units and 15% above that, of total project costs less land, existing structures, the fee itself, consultant fees and reserves. Not permitted on acquisition costs. Iowa does not score lower fees.

criteria.heading: Builder and general contractor fee limit
criteria.quote: Builder and general contractor fees shall be limited to a total

criteria.heading: Deferred developer fee limit
criteria.quote: Deferred Developer fees cannot exceed 50% of the total Developer fee

criteria.heading: Minimum debt service coverage
criteria.quote: The Application may not show DSCR as less than

criteria.heading: Replacement reserves
criteria.quote: All Family Projects shall budget replacement reserves of $350 per Unit per year,
criteria.note: Senior projects $300, or flat $435 family and $375 senior.
